Container.Name: vpn-sentinel-server
Container.Overview: VPNSentinel server: collects keepalives from VPNSentinel clients running inside your VPN containers, shows a traffic-light dashboard (green: routing through the VPN, yellow: DNS leaking, red: VPN bypass) and sends Telegram alerts. Set an API key and give the same key to every client. With an empty key the server runs with authentication disabled. Client status is kept in memory only: restarting this container forgets all clients until their next keepalive (every 5 minutes by default). To monitor a client, install vpn-sentinel-client next to your VPN container and point its server URL at this container's mapped API port.

Config.Name: API port
Config.Description: Port clients send keepalives to. Use this port in the client server URL.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: Shared secret the clients must send. Required: with an empty key the server runs with authentication disabled.

Config.Name: Telegram bot token
Config.Description: Optional. Telegram alerts are enabled when both the token and the chat ID are set.

Config.Name: Telegram chat ID
Config.Description: Optional. Chat that receives the alerts.

Config.Name: Metrics token
Config.Description: Optional. When set, /metrics on the health port requires Authorization: Bearer with this value.

Config.Name: API path
Config.Description: API path prefix. Must match the clients.

Config.Name: Web dashboard enabled
Config.Description: Set to false to turn the dashboard off.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone for log timestamps, for example Europe/Rome.
